1: // Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

4: package terraform
5: 
6: import (
7: 	"log"
8: 
9: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/addrs"
10: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/configs"
11: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/dag"
12: )
13: 
14: // GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig is an interface that must be implemented by nodes
15: // that want resource configurations attached.
16: type GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig interface {
17: 	GraphNodeConfigResource
18: 
19: 	// Sets the configuration, either to a present resource block or to
20: 	// a "removed" block commemorating a resource that has since been
21: 	// removed. Callers should always leave at least one of these
22: 	// arguments set to nil.
23: 	AttachResourceConfig(*configs.Resource, *configs.Removed)
24: }
25: 
26: // AttachResourceConfigTransformer goes through the graph and attaches
27: // resource configuration structures to nodes that implement
28: // GraphNodeAttachManagedResourceConfig or GraphNodeAttachDataResourceConfig.
29: //
30: // The attached configuration structures are directly from the configuration.
31: // If they're going to be modified, a copy should be made.
32: type AttachResourceConfigTransformer struct {
33: 	Config *configs.Config // Config is the root node in the config tree
34: }
35: 
36: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) Transform(g *Graph) error {
37: 
38: 	// Go through and find GraphNodeAttachResource
39: 	for _, v := range g.Vertices() {
40: 		// Only care about GraphNodeAttachResource implementations
41: 		arn, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig)
42: 		if !ok {
43: 			continue
44: 		}
45: 
46: 		// Determine what we're looking for
47: 		addr := arn.ResourceAddr()
48: 
49: 		// Get the configuration.
50: 		config := t.Config.Descendent(addr.Module)
51: 
52: 		if config == nil {
53: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q (%T) has no configuration available", dag.VertexName(v), v)
54: 			continue
55: 		}
56: 
57: 		if r := config.Module.ResourceByAddr(addr.Resource); r != nil {
58: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) config from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
59: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(r, nil)
60: 			if t.hasConfigConditions(addr.Module, addr.Resource) {
61: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q has configuration conditions", dag.VertexName(v))
62: 			}
63: 			if gnapmc, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachProviderMetaConfigs); ok {
64: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching provider meta configs to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
65: 				if config.Module.ProviderMetas != nil {
66: 					gnapmc.AttachProviderMetaConfigs(config.Module.ProviderMetas)
67: 				} else {
68: 					log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: no provider meta configs available to attach to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
69: 				}
70: 			}
71: 		}
72: 
73: 		for _, r := range config.Module.Removed {
74: 			crAddr, ok := r.From.RelSubject.(addrs.ConfigResource)
75: 			if !ok {
76: 				// Not for a resource at all, so can't possibly match
77: 				continue
78: 			}
79: 			rAddr := crAddr.Resource
80: 			if rAddr != addr.Resource {
81: 				// Not the same resource
82: 				continue
83: 			}
84: 
85: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) removed block from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
86: 
87: 			// Validation ensures that there can't be both a resource/data block
88: 			// and a removed block referring to the same configuration, so
89: 			// we can assume that this isn't clobbering a non-removed resource
90: 			// configuration we already attached above.
91: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(nil, r)
92: 		}
93: 	}
94: 
95: 	return nil
96: }
97: 
98: // hasConfigConditions reports whether the configuration for the given resource
99: // declares preconditions or postconditions. The lookup walks the module tree
100: // owned by the attached configuration, so this transformer can answer the same
101: // question while attaching resource configuration to the graph.
102: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) hasConfigConditions(module addrs.Module, resource addrs.Resource) bool {
103: 	if t.Config == nil {
104: 		return false
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	cfg := t.Config
108: 	for _, name := range module {
109: 		child, ok := cfg.Children[name]
110: 		if !ok || child == nil {
111: 			return false
112: 		}
113: 		cfg = child
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	if !cfg.Path.Equal(module) {
117: 		return false
118: 	}
119: 
120: 	mod := cfg.Module
121: 	if mod == nil {
122: 		return false
123: 	}
124: 
125: 	key := resource.String()
126: 	res := mod.ManagedResources[key]
127: 	if res == nil {
128: 		res = mod.DataResources[key]
129: 	}
130: 	if res == nil {
131: 		return false
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	switch res.Mode {
135: 	case addrs.ManagedResourceMode, addrs.DataResourceMode:
136: 		return len(res.Preconditions) > 0 || len(res.Postconditions) > 0
137: 	default:
138: 		return false
139: 	}
140: }

1: // Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

3: 
4: package terraform
5: 
6: import (
7: 	"log"
8: 
9: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/addrs"
10: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/configs"
11: 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform/internal/dag"
12: )
13: 
14: // GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig is an interface that must be implemented by nodes
15: // that want resource configurations attached.
16: type GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig interface {
17: 	GraphNodeConfigResource
18: 
19: 	// Sets the configuration, either to a present resource block or to
20: 	// a "removed" block commemorating a resource that has since been
21: 	// removed. Callers should always leave at least one of these
22: 	// arguments set to nil.
23: 	AttachResourceConfig(*configs.Resource, *configs.Removed)
24: }
25: 
26: // AttachResourceConfigTransformer goes through the graph and attaches
27: // resource configuration structures to nodes that implement
28: // GraphNodeAttachManagedResourceConfig or GraphNodeAttachDataResourceConfig.
29: //
30: // The attached configuration structures are directly from the configuration.
31: // If they're going to be modified, a copy should be made.
32: type AttachResourceConfigTransformer struct {
33: 	Config *configs.Config // Config is the root node in the config tree
34: }
35: 
36: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) Transform(g *Graph) error {
37: 	// Collect removed blocks to attach to any resources. These are collected
38: 	// independently because removed blocks may live in a parent module of the
39: 	// resource referenced.
40: 	removed := addrs.MakeMap[addrs.ConfigResource, *configs.Removed]()
41: 	t.Config.DeepEach(func(c *configs.Config) {
42: 		for _, r := range c.Module.Removed {
43: 			crAddr, ok := r.From.RelSubject.(addrs.ConfigResource)
44: 			if !ok {
45: 				// Not for a resource at all, so can't possibly match
46: 				continue
47: 			}
48: 			removed.Put(crAddr, r)
49: 		}
50: 	})
51: 
52: 	// Go through and find GraphNodeAttachResource
53: 	for _, v := range g.Vertices() {
54: 		// Only care about GraphNodeAttachResource implementations
55: 		arn, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig)
56: 		if !ok {
57: 			continue
58: 		}
59: 
60: 		// Determine what we're looking for
61: 		addr := arn.ResourceAddr()
62: 
63: 		if r, ok := removed.Get(addr); ok {
64: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) removed block from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
65: 
66: 			// Validation ensures that there can't be both a resource/data block
67: 			// and a removed block referring to the same configuration, so
68: 			// we can assume that this isn't clobbering a non-removed resource
69: 			// configuration we already attached above.
70: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(nil, r)
71: 		}
72: 
73: 		// Get the configuration.
74: 		config := t.Config.Descendent(addr.Module)
75: 
76: 		if config == nil {
77: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q (%T) has no configuration available", dag.VertexName(v), v)
78: 			continue
79: 		}
80: 
81: 		if r := config.Module.ResourceByAddr(addr.Resource); r != nil {
82: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) config from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)
83: 			arn.AttachResourceConfig(r, nil)
84: 			if t.hasConfigConditions(addr.Module, addr.Resource) {
85: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: %q has configuration conditions", dag.VertexName(v))
86: 			}
87: 			if gnapmc, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachProviderMetaConfigs); ok {
88: 				log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching provider meta configs to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
89: 				if config.Module.ProviderMetas != nil {
90: 					gnapmc.AttachProviderMetaConfigs(config.Module.ProviderMetas)
91: 				} else {
92: 					log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: no provider meta configs available to attach to %s", dag.VertexName(v))
93: 				}
94: 			}
95: 		}
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	return nil
99: }
100: 
101: // hasConfigConditions reports whether the configuration for the given resource
102: // declares preconditions or postconditions. The lookup walks the module tree
103: // owned by the attached configuration, so this transformer can answer the same
104: // question while attaching resource configuration to the graph.
105: func (t *AttachResourceConfigTransformer) hasConfigConditions(module addrs.Module, resource addrs.Resource) bool {
106: 	if t.Config == nil {
107: 		return false
108: 	}
109: 
110: 	cfg := t.Config
111: 	for _, name := range module {
112: 		child, ok := cfg.Children[name]
113: 		if !ok || child == nil {
114: 			return false
115: 		}
116: 		cfg = child
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	if !cfg.Path.Equal(module) {
120: 		return false
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	mod := cfg.Module
124: 	if mod == nil {
125: 		return false
126: 	}
127: 
128: 	key := resource.String()
129: 	res := mod.ManagedResources[key]
130: 	if res == nil {
131: 		res = mod.DataResources[key]
132: 	}
133: 	if res == nil {
134: 		return false
135: 	}
136: 
137: 	switch res.Mode {
138: 	case addrs.ManagedResourceMode, addrs.DataResourceMode:
139: 		return len(res.Preconditions) > 0 || len(res.Postconditions) > 0
140: 	default:
141: 		return false
142: 	}
143: }

part.text:
Done. The fix is in `internal/terraform/transform_attach_config_resource.go:36`.

**Root cause:** `AttachResourceConfigTransformer` only searched for `removed` blocks within the same module as the target resource (`t.Config.Descendent(addr.Module).Module.Removed`). A `removed` block declared in the root module targeting `module.foo.<resource>` lives in the root config, so its destroy provisioners were never attached to the resource's graph node — and destroy-time provisioners were silently skipped.

**Fix:** the transformer now collects all `removed` blocks across the entire config tree (`t.Config.DeepEach`) into a map keyed by `addrs.ConfigResource`, then attaches the matching one to each resource node regardless of which module the block was declared in.

Verified with `TestContext2Apply_provisionerDestroyRemoved` (was failing with "provisioner not invoked", now passes), plus the full `internal/terraform` and `internal/configs` test suites — all pass.
